Recognise and type מ, נ, ת and ל from their sounds.
Recover the shape through a familiar image, then retrieve the sound without the image.
SOURCES / ADAPTATION: Presentation slides 6 and 10; Hebleo Mnemonics slides 2 and 6; current A2 row 5. Earlier first20 MNT prose adapted, with ל added and final forms removed.

DESIGN DECISIONS: Preserve Guy’s mountain-climber, nose, tripping and ladle anchors. Introduce all four letters together before mixed retrieval; the earlier two-pair split is removed. Use the original drawings and human sound recordings. No final-form teaching or extra vocabulary in this lesson.
Learn — exact text and embedded interactions
Screen 1: Four shapes, four sounds · MNTL-A2.learn.mem-nun
מ represents /m/, the sound at the start of
נ represents /n/, the sound at the start of
ת represents /t/, as at the start of tripping. Its name is Tav.
ל represents /l/, as at the start of ladle. Its name is Lamed.

Listen to each sound and look at its letter. The mountain-climber, nose, tripping and ladle pictures connect each printed shape to a familiar word that begins with its sound. You do not need to memorise the letter names yet.
[AUTHOR INSTRUCTION] AUDIO MNTL-M, MNTL-N, MNTL-T and MNTL-L: human recordings of /m/, /n/, /t/ and /l/. Play individually on request, without an added vowel. Present all four on this page.

[AUTHOR INSTRUCTION] IMAGE MNTL-M, MNTL-N, MNTL-T and MNTL-L: Guy’s original mountain-climber, nose, tripping and ladle drawings, each paired with the exact block letter. Preserve the original drawings. Show all four together; let the learner inspect and replay each at their own pace.
Screen 2: Try without the pictures · MNTL-A2.learn.pair-retrieve
Now try recognising a letter without its picture. If you need help, bring the familiar image back to mind.
FEEDBACK after “מ”: מ represents /m/. The sound you heard was /n/.
FEEDBACK after “נ”: Yes: נ represents /n/, as in nose.

[AUTHOR INSTRUCTION] Add option-specific feedback for ת and ל: “ת represents /t/. The sound you heard was /n/.” / “ל represents /l/. The sound you heard was /n/.” The four-letter teaching page comes before this first question.
Screen 3: Make the shape yourself · MNTL-A2.learn.typing
Choose the matching printed letter on the Hebrew keyboard. You may use the on-screen keyboard.
Copying a visible shape helps you locate its key. In the next exercise, the shape will be hidden so that you can try to recall it.
[PLACEHOLDER / AUTHOR INSTRUCTION] KEYBOARD: highlight the matching key only during copying. Hide the highlight for recall questions.
FEEDBACK: Correct: ל. Use the same printed form; handwriting is not required.
FEEDBACK after “נ”: נ is /n/. Think of tripping for /t/.
FEEDBACK after “מ”: מ is /m/. Think of tripping for /t/.
FEEDBACK after “ל”: ל is /l/. Think of tripping for /t/.
Vocabulary — current learner display and author reference
No new vocabulary entries in this lesson. Letter shapes, sounds or memory materials are taught in Learn and practised in the exercises; do not add a lexical quota.
Match each sound to its printed letter.
FEEDBACK: מ = /m/, נ = /n/, ת = /t/, ל = /l/. Replay a missed sound, then retry it without the mnemonic.
Listen and type the printed letter.
FEEDBACK: The matching letter is מ; its sound is /m/.
Listen and type the printed letter.
FEEDBACK: The matching letter is ל; its sound is /l/.
Read the sounds of these letters aloud: ל  מ  ת  נ.
FEEDBACK: Reveal the four individual sound buttons and compare one at a time. This is self-check, not automatic pronunciation scoring.
You can now connect four printed letters to their sounds. Next, you will see how Hebrew arranges them and what happens to מ and נ at the end of a word.
Supply the four original mnemonic drawings and isolated consonant recordings, avoiding an added vowel after the consonant.
